newsitem.title: GERMANY: China soymeal demand seen underpinning 96/97 price.
newsitem.headline: China soymeal demand seen underpinning 96/97 price.

text.p: Asian soymeal demand, led by China, would underpin prices at least in the first half of the 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) season, independent newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.
But soymeal could be vulnerable to a spill-over effect from lower grain prices.
Imports by South Korea were likely to decline and demand elsewhere in the Far East could also weaken but huge Chinese requirements outweighed these factors.
China's soymeal imports in 96/97 were forecast at 2.65 millio tonnes versus 1.6 million in the 95/96 season.
Soymeal exports by the four leading suppliers U.S., Argentina, Brazil and India to Asia nearly doubled to a historic high of 8.4 million tonnes in 1995/96.

The unexpected rise resulted in falls elsewhere, notably the EU, where shipments from the four suppliers were down 22 percent from a year earlier in January-September 1996 at 2.4 million tonnes. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
